title: Traditional Chinese Hundred-Ke Clock
intro: This clock divides the local civil day into exactly one hundred equal ke, a traditional Chinese time division.
structure: One ke is 1/100 of a nominal 24-hour day: 864 ordinary seconds, or 14 minutes 24 seconds. The display counts completed units from 00 to 99 and rolls over at local midnight.
example: Midnight is 00 ke, 06:00 is 25 ke, noon is 50 ke and 18:00 is 75 ke. At 00:14:24 the reading advances from 00 to 01.
history: The hundred-ke division is a historical Chinese convention associated with systems such as water clocks. Other periods employed differing counts, including 96-ke schemes; they are not interchangeable with this model.
model: The provider floor-divides the positive local civil microsecond phase by 864000000. It displays two decimal digits with a localised unit label (Chinese/Japanese character, Russian form, or romanised ke). Next-update delay is the remaining microseconds before the next ke boundary, rounded up to milliseconds.
limits: This is a Han-era-style mathematical projection using modern supplied civil offset, not a reconstruction of every historical time system or an observed water-clock rate. The seconds toggle does not add finer units; location coordinates are not needed.
